chapter: Boots and His Buddies and Wild Cherry
title: How Wild Cherry's high-note solo took shape at rehearsal
summary: The written part was too high, so Harris and Siki Collins played with it at his house, reworking the tune before rehearsal.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Well that's the record that made Boots and that's the record of course that made me and myself at the same time made Boots. We had no idea that was going to be a hit. I'll tell you how that came about. We had some music there with this tune Cherry, they called it Cherry but it was written so doggone high it was still up around C and above all the time. Really we couldn't play it. Didn't have anybody in the band could reach those high notes except the third man and he couldn't have the first. And I could make, I could hit those notes but I couldn't play up there. Well they were going to have rehearsal at my house and Sy Kye Collins, this boy that had played with Troy, had cut out from Troy's band and came over to Boots' band and he took
up with me, he liked to hang around my house all the time.

We'd always get our horns out and sit around there puff and blow, just bow and set without any piano coming or anything. He'd sit there and blow. He'd blow something, I'd blow something. Enjoyed that. So before rehearsal we got home out of that day and I started playing around this thing Cherry. Well I blew till my lips, my lips was chopped and was gone and my chops was gone and I'd come back downstairs and I went to play and instead of making it like they had it written I'd come and put my lip in it. And he says, do that again. Well I did it, when I got to do it again, well he hit the bridge, he took the bridge, he takes that bridge, goes on through it and I took it again. He says, you know that sounds good like that. He said, how about we just, let's take it down again. I said, okay, you like that?
He said, man, I think it stinks. He said, no, that sounds good, you want some handle?
Well all right, when Booth came I had wrote an arrangement on Tiger Rag, well I insisted on him playing, let's play this Tiger. Tip
